Operation

Genome alignment

Arrange per-sample genome sequences so that equivalent positions line up across every sample.

Inputs

  • Per-sample genome sequences

Outputs

  • Whole-genome alignment (FASTA)

An alignment places homologous positions from every sample in the same column, so differences between samples can be counted and modeled. It is needed whenever the previous step produced one sequence per sample rather than an alignment.

Methods 1

  • Multiple sequence alignment

    Align per-sample genome sequences so equivalent positions line up, optionally anchored to a reference to standardize coordinates.

    Use when

    • You have one genome sequence per sample (or per segment), from consensus calling or curated de novo assemblies.
    • Indels should be kept in the alignment.
    • You want positions reported in standard reference coordinates. Use the reference-guided mode described below.

    MAFFT · Nextclade (reference-guided) · minimap2 + gofasta (reference-guided)
